Task: Outline and partially script a 15-minute educational video on climate change.

Below is a complete, detailed outline—plus a partially-scripted sample of key portions—for a 15-minute educational video on climate change.  
(The video is assumed to be aimed at a general audience—teen and adult learners—with lively visuals, simple graphics, short on-screen text, light motion graphics, and a presenter on camera.)

────────────────────────────────────────
A. TOP-LEVEL VIDEO STRUCTURE (15:00)
────────────────────────────────────────
00:00–00:45  Cold-open “hook” & title  
00:45–02:15  Section 1  • What IS climate change?  
02:15–04:15  Section 2  • How do we know it’s happening?  
04:15–07:15  Section 3  • Major causes (focus on greenhouse gases)  
07:15–09:30  Section 4  • Current & future impacts (global + local)  
09:30–12:00  Section 5  • Solutions you’ve heard of—and some you haven’t  
12:00–14:30  Section 6  • What can individuals, schools & communities do?  
14:30–15:00  Wrap-up, call-to-action & end-screen

Total runtime ≈ 15:00

────────────────────────────────────────
B. DETAILED OUTLINE & VISUAL NOTES
────────────────────────────────────────
0) STYLE NOTES
• Presenter stands in bright, natural-light studio; large screen behind for graphics.  
• Tone: energetic but trustworthy; mix of talking-head, animated infographics, quick field clips.  
• Text on screen never >12 words; key numbers reinforced with icons.  
• Subtle background track; ducked under dialogue.  

1) OPENING HOOK (0:00–0:30)
Visual: Rapid montage—flooded street → blazing wildfire → satellite of shrinking ice → children installing solar panels on school roof.  
Presenter VO: “From record-breaking floods to solar panels popping up in places you’d least expect, our planet is telling a story—one that affects every one of us.”  
On-screen text: “CLIMATE CHANGE: 15 minutes to understand—and act.”

Cut to TITLE CARD (0:30–0:45)  
Animated title: “Climate Change—The Basics, The Impacts, The Solutions” + upbeat stinger.

2) SECTION 1 – WHAT IS CLIMATE CHANGE? (0:45–2:15)
Key points  
• Weather vs. climate (30-year averages)  
• Natural vs. human-driven change  
• Greenhouse effect in 20 seconds  

Visuals  
• Split-screen of weather icons → 30-yr calendar.  
• Simple animation: sunlight → Earth → heat trapped by greenhouse-gas layer.  

Sample script excerpt  
Presenter: “Imagine Earth wrapped in an invisible blanket. A blanket is great on a cold night; but pile on too many and you start to sweat. Since the Industrial Revolution, we’ve been adding blanket after blanket, trapping heat that used to escape to space.”

3) SECTION 2 – HOW DO WE KNOW? (2:15–4:15)
Key points  
• Thermometer records since 1880  
• Ice cores & CO₂ ‘time capsules’  
• Ocean heat content → >90 % of warming  
• Multiple, independent lines of evidence  

Visuals  
• Animated graph: global temp ↑ 1.2 °C.  
• Drilling ice core footage; bubbles pop → CO₂ meter.  
• Stacked bars: atmosphere vs. ocean heat uptake.  

Quick quiz pop-up: “True or false: Satellites have tracked sea-level rise since 1993?” (Answer revealed 5 s later.)

4) SECTION 3 – CAUSES (4:15–7:15)
Key points  
• CO₂ from fossil fuels ≈ 75 % of GHGs  
• Methane (CH₄) & nitrous oxide (N₂O) basics  
• Land-use change & deforestation = ≈10 %  
• Feedback loops (albedo, thawing permafrost) short intro  

Visuals  
• Pie chart of emissions by sector (energy, agriculture, industry, transport).  
• Side-by-side: coal plant plume vs. cows burping methane bubble.  
• Permafrost map turning red.  

Short field insert (pre-recorded): 10-s drone shot of clear-cut forest.  

5) SECTION 4 – IMPACTS (7:15–9:30)
Key points  
• Extreme weather: heatwaves, intense rainfall, megafires  
• Sea-level rise / coastal risk  
• Food & water security  
• Health & economic costs  
• Disproportionate effects on vulnerable communities  

Visuals  
• Map animation: storm tracks intensify 1950-2025.  
• Before/after photo slider: glacier retreat.  
• Lower-third shows cost: “US weather disasters 2023: $90 billion.”  

Human story vignette (20 s): Farmer adjusting irrigation, says: “Rainfall now comes in bursts—too much or not at all.”

6) SECTION 5 – SOLUTIONS (9:30–12:00)
Key points  
• Mitigation vs. adaptation  
• Big three pillars: Clean energy, efficiency, protect nature  
• Exciting newcomers: direct-air capture, green hydrogen, regenerative ag  
• Co-benefits: cleaner air, jobs, biodiversity  

Visuals  
• World map lights up with wind/solar icons.  
• Graph: price of solar panels 1976-2024 nose-dives 99 %.  
• 3-D render: DAC plant “vacuuming” CO₂.  
Cut-in stat bar: “Every $1 invested in adaptation → $4 saved in damages (World Bank).”

7) SECTION 6 – WHAT CAN YOU DO? (12:00–14:30)
Key points  
• “Big four” personal levers: vote, talk, eat, travel  
• Community projects: school solar, tree-planting, local climate plans  
• Careers & skills of the future  
Interactive challenge: “Pick ONE action today & tag us #MyClimateMinute.”  

Visuals  
• Fast collage: students lobbying, induction cooktop, bike commute, community garden.  
• On-screen checklist boxes that tick as options named.  

Sample script excerpt  
Presenter: “Maybe you can’t build an offshore wind farm—but you can choose leaders who will. Maybe you’re not ready for an EV, but cutting just one flight can save half a tonne of CO₂.”

8) WRAP-UP & CTA (14:30–15:00)
• Recap 3-word mantra on screen: “Understand. Share. Act.”  
• URL & QR-code to free resources / lesson plan.  
• End-screen: subscribe, share, playlist of deeper-dive videos.

────────────────────────────────────────
C. PARTIAL SCRIPT (SELECTED SECTIONS, READY FOR TELEPROMPTER)
────────────────────────────────────────
[OPENING HOOK 0:00–0:30]

[Montage B-roll. Upbeat tempo.]

PRESENTER (V.O.):  
“Floods that shut down entire cities… wildfires visible from space… but also, breakthroughs in clean energy happening faster than anyone predicted. Welcome to the story of climate change—written by 8 billion of us, day by day.”

[Cut to studio, Presenter on-camera.]

PRESENTER:  
“In the next fifteen minutes, you’ll learn what climate change really means, how we know it’s real, what it’s already doing to our world, and—most important—what solutions are on the table. Ready? Let’s jump in.”

[SECTION 1 0:45–1:30]

Graphic pops up: “Weather ≠ Climate”

PRESENTER:  
“First, definitions. Weather is whether you need an umbrella today; climate is whether you usually need one in June. Scientists average at least thirty years of weather data to define a region’s climate.”

[Beat, full-screen animation of greenhouse effect.]

PRESENTER:  
“Earth naturally traps some of the Sun’s heat—without this greenhouse effect we’d freeze at –18 °C. The problem? Humans are turbo-charging that effect by adding billions of tonnes of heat-trapping gases.”

[SECTION 2 – Ice cores 3:05–3:35]

[Arctic footage; ice core lab.]

PRESENTER:  
“Deep inside Greenland’s ice lie bubbles of ancient air—literal samples of Earth’s atmosphere going back 800-thousand years. When scientists measure the CO₂ in those bubbles, they find a steady rhythm… until the last century, when the graph shoots up like a hockey stick.”

[Cut to line graph; stinger SFX.]

PRESENTER:  
“That spike matches the rise of coal, oil and natural gas.”

[SECTION 4 – Impacts clip 7:50–8:05]

PRESENTER stands by large screen; wildfire footage playing.

PRESENTER:  
“Wildfires have always happened, but in places like California and Australia their season is now nearly twice as long, and the fires burn hotter. Hotter air pulls moisture from plants, turning forests into tinder.”

[SECTION 5 – Solutions 10:10–10:40]

[Animation: cost curve for solar.]

PRESENTER:  
“Here’s some good news: in the 1970s a solar watt cost about $100. Today? Under 20 cents. That’s like a laptop dropping from three million dollars to thirty bucks.”

[Quick cut: wind farm.]

PRESENTER:  
“Add smart policies, and renewable energy can now out-compete fossil fuels in most regions—without subsidies.”

[SECTION 6 – Personal action 13:20–13:50]

PRESENTER:  
“Think individual actions don’t matter? Peer-reviewed studies show that simply talking about climate with friends is one of the fastest ways to raise public support for solutions. Conversation = catalyst.”

[Pull out whiteboard with 4 icons: ballot box, speech bubble, fork, suitcase.]

PRESENTER:  
“Vote, talk, eat more plants, and rethink how we move around. Pick one to start.”

[WRAP 14:30–15:00]

[Presenter center frame; minimal motion graphic of Earth rotating.]

PRESENTER:  
“Climate change is here—but so are solutions. Understand the science, share what you learn, and act where you can. Links are in the description. I’m [Name]; thanks for spending your climate minute.”

[END-SCREEN with social links, resource QR, subscribe button.]

────────────────────────────────────────
D. ASSET & PRODUCTION CHECKLIST
────────────────────────────────────────
• 10 royalty-free video clips (flood, fire, glacier retreat, wind farm, etc.)  
• 8 custom animated infographics (temperature chart, emissions pie, cost curve, etc.)  
• Presenter mic + teleprompter script (above)  
• Background music track (15-min license, BPM ≈ 100, loopable)  
• Sound effects: whoosh for transitions, pop for quiz answer  
• Thumbnail concept: Presenter holding infrared thermometer against Earth graphic, big text “Climate in 15 min?”  

────────────────────────────────────────
E. OPTIONAL EXTENSIONS
────────────────────────────────────────
• Interactive version with embedded quizzes (H5P / Edpuzzle).  
• B-roll inserts from local community climate projects for regional versions.  
• Teacher worksheet: vocabulary list, comprehension questions, extension activity.

────────────────────────────────────────
That completes the comprehensive outline and sample scripting needed to produce an engaging, 15-minute educational video on climate change.
